references.text: The Lord tells Moses in Midian that he may return to Egypt because those who sought to kill him are dead, referring back to Pharaoh's attempt on his life.
Moses mentions his father-in-law Hobab from Midian, pointing to his time in Midian after fleeing from Egypt.
Midian is mentioned as one of Abraham's sons through Keturah, explaining the origin of the Midianites where Moses found refuge.
Jacob meets Rachel at the well, a similar motif where a foreign man meets his future wife at a well.
Abraham's servant meets Rebekah at the well, a recurring biblical theme where important encounters take place at wells.
Elijah flees from Jezebel who seeks to kill him, paralleling Moses fleeing from Pharaoh.
Stephen refers directly to this event in his speech, recounting how Moses fled and became a stranger in Midian.
The Letter to the Hebrews notes that by faith Moses left Egypt without fearing the king's anger, relating to his flight.
Thematic parallel: A prophetic leader flees to Egypt to escape the king's attempt on his life.
